## Versioning & stability

* The API is **path-versioned** (`/api/v1`). When it reaches general
 availabilit
y, breaking changes will require a new version path.\n* **During the preview**, breaking changes to v1 may still happen; we'll not
e\n them in the [changelog](https://docs.mcpjam.com/changelog/overview.md).\n* **Additive changes** — new endpoints, new optional
request fields, new\n response fields, new error codes — are considered non-breaking and can ship\n at any time. Write clients

that ignore unknown fields.
* Error **codes** are stable identifiers; error **messages** are not.

### Renamed surfaces

Thre
e nouns this API used are now what the product calls them: `scenario` is\n**study**, `journey` is **goal**, and `wave` is **swarm

run**. The paths, the
operation names, the SDK types and the noun-bearing response fields all moved:

| Was | Is |
| - | - |
| `/projects/{projectId}/scenarios[/{scenarioId}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/studies[/{studyId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/user-
testing/scenarios/{scenarioId}/…` | `/projects/{projectId}/studies/{studyId}/…` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/environments/{environm
entId}/scenario` | `.../environments/{environmentId}/study` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys[/{journeyId}]` | `/projects/{proj
ectId}/goals[/{goalId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journey-runs/{runId}` | `/projects/{projectId}/goal-runs/{runId}` |\n| `/proj
ects/{projectId}/journeys-overview`, `.../journey-findings` | `.../goals-overview`, `.../goal-findings` |\n| `/projects/{projectId
}/waves/{waveId}/insights` | `/projects/{projectId}/swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` |\n\nResponse fields followed their nouns: `

scenarioId` → `studyId`, `journeyId` →
`goalId`, `waveId` → `swarmRunId`, and `sessionsPerTarget` → `iterations`.

Two reads be
came one: `get_scenario` served the execution settings and\n`get_user_testing_scenario` served the environment id and the insights
\nenvelope. `get_study` returns both, and the two caller-dependent fields are\nabsent rather than null when you may not have them.

**Every old path still works** and is unchanged, including its old response
spellings. Each one answers with `Deprecation: tr
ue` and a `Link` header naming\nits successor. They are undocumented on purpose — the spec is what a new\nintegration reads — and

they are removed at general availability.

A handful of operations kept their names through the rename and so have no
deprecate
d twin to hold the old field spellings. `get_swarms_overview`,\n`create_swarm` and `update_swarm` emit both and accept either — ne

ver both in
one request — until general availability.

### Vocabulary

A name can move behind an alias; a VALUE cannot. `sour
ceType` is one field with\none string in it, and a client switching on `\"scenario\"` has no second name to\nfall back to. So the

values negotiate.

Send `x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary: 2` and the renamed values read canonically:

| Field | Vocabulary 1 | Vocabu

lary 2 |
| - | - | - |
| session `sourceType` | `scenario` | `study` |
| session `parentRef.kind` | `scenario`, `journeyRun` |
`study`, `goalRun` |\n| session `parentRef` ids | `scenarioId`, `journeyRunId`, `journeyRefId` | `studyId`, `goalRunId`, `goalRefI
d` |\n| share `resourceType` (field AND path segment) | `scenario` | `study` |\n| trace-destination `sourceTypes` | `scenario` | `

study` |

Absent means `1`, which is byte-for-byte today's contract. Any other value is a
`400`. On the way IN, a vocabulary-2
request may name a filter or a path segment\nby either spelling; a vocabulary-1 request may use only the legacy one, because\na bo
undary that accepts a spelling it does not announce is one two\nimplementations can disagree about. A response that varies by voca

bulary sends
`Vary: x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary`.

This is a **separate header** from `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary`, which is
eval-sc
oped by name and moves on its own schedule. A deployment may speak one\nand not the other, so read\n`GET /projects/{projectId}/cap
abilities` — `apiVocabulary` and `vocabulary` are\ntwo blocks — before sending either. With the SDK:\n`new PlatformApiClient({ …,

apiVocabulary: 2 })`, or
`client.withApiVocabulary(2)` on one you already hold.

Permalink resource types are the exception tha
t proves the rule: `study` and\n`goal_run` are the canonical keys, `user_testing_scenario` and `journey_run`\nstill resolve to the
same routes, and which one a response carries follows the\nOPERATION rather than the header — a renamed operation derives the can

onical
key, its deprecated twin the old one. `capabilities.apiVocabulary.resourceTypes`
lists both.

### Browser tools on chat

sessions

> [!NOTE]
>
> Hosted browser availability depends on the account and deployment. The browser workspace must be enab
led to open the live pane in the Playground.\n\n`POST /chat-sessions/messages` accepts an optional `browser: { policy?, profileId?
}`. Attach it on every turn that should browse. The initial grant and profile are fixed; the current host policy and pinned read-
only mode can narrow the effective permissions. Responses and traces include the read-only `chatSessionId`, browser metadata, and

screenshot URLs without inline image data.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| - | - | - |
| POST | `/chat-sessions/browser` | Crea
te an empty API session and its browser with `projectId`, `policy`, optional `profileId`, and a stable `idempotencyKey`. |\n| POST
| `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/open` | Open or wake the session browser. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/c
ommand` | Execute a browser command under the session policy with a stable `commandId`. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/br
owser/note` | Append a command-ledger note. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/trace` | Read command receipts and scr
eenshot evidence. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/artifact` | Resolve a command screenshot URL. |\n| POST | `/chat
-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/close` | Release the session desktop. |\n\nOnly the owning user can drive an API session's browser.
All inputs use the public `sessionId`; conversation and browser identifiers in responses are informational. Capacity refusals befo
re execution release the turn lease so the same idempotency key can be retried. An execution with an unknown outcome must be inspe

cted before attempting a new action.
